Model tier.d: A named size level within a model family, such as Claude's Haiku, Sonnet, Opus and Fable. Higher tiers are usually more capable but slower and more expensive.

Model snapshot.d: One fixed, frozen version of a model, identified by an exact model ID. Calling the same snapshot later gives you the same model.

Deprecation.d: The stage where a model still works but has a published date after which it will be retired and stop answering.

Distillation.d: Training a smaller 'student' model to imitate a larger 'teacher' model, so the small model gains much of the large one's skill at lower running cost.

Mixture of Experts.d: A model design with many expert sub-networks and a router that uses only a few of them for each token, so total size can be huge while cost per token stays lower. Often shortened to MoE.

Active parameters.d: In a Mixture of Experts model, the parameters actually used to process each token, as opposed to the model's total parameter count.

Proprietary model.d: A model whose weights are kept private by its maker; you can only use it through the maker's app, API or approved cloud partners.

Open source AI.d: Under the Open Source Initiative's 2024 definition, an AI system released with its weights, complete training and running code, and detailed training-data information, under terms allowing use, study, modification and sharing.

Permissive licence.d: A licence such as Apache 2.0 or MIT that allows commercial use, modification and redistribution with few conditions, mainly keeping the notices.

Acceptable use policy.d: A document from a model or service provider listing the uses that are forbidden. Licences and terms often require you to follow it.

Self-hosting.d: Running a model on hardware you control (your own computer, servers or cloud account) instead of calling a vendor's API.

Quantisation.d: Storing a model's numbers with fewer bits (for example 8-bit or 4-bit instead of 16-bit) so it needs less memory and runs faster, usually with a small loss of quality.

Model card.d: A short document published with a model describing who made it, its intended uses, how it was evaluated, its results, risks and limits.

System card.d: A detailed report a lab publishes with a major model release, covering capabilities, safety testing, red-teaming, safeguards and the deployment decision.

Leaderboard.d: A public ranking of models by their scores on a benchmark or on human preference votes.

Cherry-picking.d: Showing only the results that look good, such as the benchmarks a model won, while leaving out the rest.

Benchmark contamination.d: When a benchmark's questions or answers have leaked into a model's training data, so it can score well by remembering rather than solving.

Benchmark saturation.d: When top models all score near the maximum on a benchmark, so it no longer separates good models from better ones.
